study_identification_part.si4_title: A multimodal neural signature of face processing in autism within the fusiform gyrus

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To characterize multimodal neural signatures of face processing within the fusiform gyrus in autism by combining normative modeling with linked independent component analysis, and to test whether multimodal components differentiate autistic from non-autistic individuals and relate to social functioning.

rci9_site_effect_handling.detail: Site was included as a covariate in Bayesian linear regression normative models alongside age and sex. Site-specific effects were modeled during normative modeling estimation. No separate batch-removal harmonization (like ComBat) was applied prior to modeling. Multi-site data acquisition used harmonized protocols and quality assurance procedures with phantoms and traveling heads to ensure standardization across six acquisition sites (KCL, RUNMC, UCAM, UMCU, UCBM, CIMH). Site effects were also tested in group comparisons showing no significant site × diagnosis interactions for IC44.
rci9_site_effect_handling.supporting_text: Here, we trained normative models using Bayesian linear regression for each brain imaging modality within the right and left FFG region of interest (ROI) independently using age, sex and scanning site as covariates. ... The results further showed that there were no significant effects of site on group-differential IC44 (site 1: t = 0.37, P = 0.71; site 2: t = 0.1, P = 0.92; site 3: t = -0.78, P = 0.43), nor were there any diagnosis by site effects (diagnosis × site 1: t = 0.96, P = 0.34; diagnosis × site 2: t = 0.76, P = 0.45; diagnosis × site 3: t = 0.1, P = 0.92).

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: One multimodal component (IC44) significantly differentiated autistic vs NAI; multimodal components outperformed unimodal in classification; in autism, multimodal components associated with social (but not nonsocial) functioning.
